evals.prompt: I need to back up every one of my LabArchives notebooks, with attachments, as archives for our records. How do I script that?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-labarchive. Authenticates via the REST API (users/user_access_info to get the UID), lists notebooks, and uses scripts/notebook_operations.py backup-all (or labapi notebook.backup()), which saves each notebook as a 7z archive with attachments by default, against the correct regional api_url; notes only the notebook owner can download a backup.

assertions.value: Obtains the UID via user_access_info and uses the notebook backup operation, defaulting to a 7z archive with attachments.

evals.prompt: Automate uploading a PDF results file as an attachment to a specific page of my LabArchives notebook, with a note timestamping the upload.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-labarchive. Attaches the PDF to the target page (nbid + page tree id pid) via entries/add_attachment — e.g. scripts/entry_operations.py upload --nbid ... --pid ... --file ... or labapi page.entries.create(AttachmentEntry, Attachment.from_file(...)) — with the timestamp recorded in the caption or a follow-up text entry (entries/add_entry). Signs requests with akid/expires/sig rather than sending the access password.

assertions.value: Uploads the PDF as an attachment entry on a LabArchives page (nbid + pid) and records the timestamp in the caption or a text entry, using signed requests.

evals.prompt: After I run a Jupyter notebook I want to push its HTML export into LabArchives as a new entry automatically. Walk me through wiring that up.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-labarchive. Routes to the third-party Jupyter integration: export the Jupyter notebook to HTML/PDF, add it to a LabArchives page as a rich-text entry (entries/add_entry, e.g. via labapi or entry_operations.py) with the .ipynb as an attachment, and record the execution timestamp and environment info in a text entry.

evals.prompt: As the LabArchives admin I want a detailed usage report of user activity across our institution for this year.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-labarchive. Uses the site_reports API (e.g. detailed_usage_report with start_date/end_date) to generate the institutional usage/activity report, noting it is an Enterprise feature.

evals.prompt: I exported one of my LabArchives notebooks to export_Lab_Notebook/ before archiving it. Without any API credentials, audit it: how many pages and entries, and are there any pages where I dumped raw data but forgot to write a note explaining it?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-labarchive on the keyless path (e.g. scripts/analyze_export.py) with no credentials: walks the exported folder tree and reports 3 pages, 2 text entries and 3 attachment entries (a .pdf, a .csv and a .tif), and flags the provenance gap at 00_Experiments/01_Run-12, which holds a raw CSV and a gel TIFF but no text entry describing them. Does not contact the LabArchives API.

assertions.value: Audits the exported tree offline, counting 3 pages / 2 text + 3 attachment entries and flagging Run-12 as the attachment-without-text provenance gap, with no API call.

evals.prompt: I'm writing a LabArchives API client in Python and the signatures keep getting rejected. I don't want to keep hammering the API with my token while I debug. How is the request signature built, and does it matter whether I use labapi or the labarchives-py wrapper?
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-labarchive and explains the signing offline: sig = base64(HMAC(access_password, akid + method_name + expires)) with expires in epoch-milliseconds, sent as the akid/expires/sig query params so the password itself is never transmitted. Crucially warns that the hash differs between clients — labapi uses HMAC-SHA512 while the git labarchives-py wrapper uses HMAC-SHA1 — so a signature valid for one may be rejected by the other; match the client to what the institution's API expects and test against the tenant. Does not require making a live call to answer.

assertions.value: Describes the akid+method+expires HMAC signature with epoch-ms expires and flags the SHA512 (labapi) vs SHA1 (labarchives-py) difference, without needing a live call.

evals.prompt: Draft the rich-text HTML for a LabArchives entry summarizing today's qPCR run (plate layout, Ct values table, a short conclusion) plus the caption I should put on the raw .eds attachment, so it's ready to push once I set up my API token.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-labarchive and drafts the entry content offline with no credentials: valid rich-text HTML for the entry (headings, a Ct-values table, a conclusion paragraph) suitable for entries/add_entry with part_type 'text entry', and a provenance caption for the .eds attachment (instrument, run date, operator, software version). Notes the entry is pushed later with page.entries.create / entries/add_entry once LA_APP_TOKEN and the access password are set, without claiming anything was uploaded.

assertions.value: Produces ready-to-push entry HTML and an attachment provenance caption offline, deferring the actual upload to the credentialed add_entry/add_attachment call.

evals.prompt: I need to register 30 DNA sequences in our Benchling registry and create matching inventory containers via the Benchling SDK.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke this skill; defers to alterlab-benchling. The platform is Benchling (registry entities, inventory containers, benchling-sdk), not the LabArchives ELN REST API.

evals.prompt: Help me publish a protocol on protocols.io with a DOI and manage its step-level comments from reviewers.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke this skill; defers to alterlab-protocolsio. The user is managing and publishing protocols on protocols.io (DOI, step comments via the v3 API), not automating a LabArchives notebook.

evals.prompt: Build the REDCap data dictionary for our trial's baseline and follow-up visits, with branching logic and date validation, and map the fields to CDISC SDTM.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke this skill; defers to alterlab-redcap-cdisc. The task is designing REDCap instruments and CDISC mappings, not moving records into or out of a LabArchives notebook.
